newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Death toll rises to 10 in Russian block explosion.
newsitem.headline: Death toll rises to 10 in Russian block explosion.

text.p: At least ten people died and six others were missing on Saturday in the rubble of an apartment block torn apart by a gas explosion in northwest Russia, Itar-Tass news agency said.

The blast on Friday in the town of Priozersk 120 km (80 miles) north of St Petersburg was so powerful that parts of the roof of the five-storey building fell through to the ground floor, the agency said.

Rescue work continued through the night in extremely cold weather, with officials expecting no one trapped inside to survive more than one night because of the temperature, a spokesman for the Emergencies Ministry said on Friday.
Nearly 500 rescuers from Russia and a small group from Finland took part in the operation, expected to be completed on Saturday, Tass said.
Interfax news agency quoted a police spokesman as saying the blast had been caused by illegal tapping into the gas supply system.

A family living in one of the flats had its gas cut off for unpaid bills in March and when cold winter came, cut into the gas main "in a flagrant breach of safety regulations," the agency quoted the spokesman as saying.

In the first 11 months of this year 13,719 people died in fires across Russia and 12,876 were injured, a 10 percent rise on the year before, Tass quoted the Interior Ministry fire fighting service as saying.
Russian firefighters complain that the number of fires in apartment blocks grows every winter as people try to produce extra heat using makeshift electric devices or gas stoves.
